exact_section.heading: Key action statements 1A–1B — acute rhinosinusitis distinction and clinical diagnosis context
exact_section.evidence_summary: Supports documenting symptom duration and pattern, purulent drainage, nasal obstruction, facial pain or pressure, worsening pattern, associated symptoms, and relevant negatives without asserting viral or bacterial diagnosis.

exact_source_references.source_organisation: American Academy of Otolaryngology–Head and Neck Surgery Foundation
exact_source_references.source_document_title: Clinical Practice Guideline: Adult Sinusitis Update

exact_section.heading: Key action statement 6 — treatment-failure or worsening reassessment
exact_section.evidence_summary: Supports interval change, persistent or worsening symptom review, clinician reassessment, and documented follow-up without changing treatment.

exact_source_references.source_organisation: American Academy of Otolaryngology–Head and Neck Surgery Foundation
exact_source_references.source_document_title: Clinical Practice Guideline: Adult Sinusitis Update

exact_section.heading: Key action statements 7A–10 — chronic distinction, objective confirmation, modifiers, testing, and polyps
exact_section.evidence_summary: Supports documenting chronic or recurrent pattern, clinician-performed nasal examination, already available endoscopy or CT, asthma, cystic fibrosis, immunocompromise, ciliary dyskinesia, allergy or immune-testing context, and presence or absence of polyps without generating testing or treatment.

exact_source_references.source_document_title: DHA Telehealth Clinical Guidelines for Virtual Management of Acute Rhinosinusitis

exact_section.heading: 5. Types; 8. Clinical History
exact_section.evidence_summary: Defines duration patterns and lists congestion, discharge, postnasal drip, dental discomfort, facial pain or pressure, fever, fatigue, cough, smell change, and headache.

exact_source_references.source_document_title: DHA Telehealth Clinical Guidelines for Virtual Management of Acute Rhinosinusitis

exact_section.heading: 9. Red Flags
exact_section.evidence_summary: Lists high fever, frontal or periorbital swelling, severe headache, meningeal or mental-status change, visual change, and persistent unilateral or bloody symptoms.

exact_source_references.source_document_title: DHA Telehealth Clinical Guidelines for Virtual Management of Acute Rhinosinusitis

exact_section.heading: 12. Investigations; 13. Referral Criteria
exact_section.evidence_summary: Limits imaging and other tests to clinician-selected contexts and lists emergency, specialist, systemic-illness, and non-response referral criteria.

exact_source_references.source_document_title: DHA Telehealth Clinical Guidelines for Virtual Management of Acute Rhinosinusitis

exact_section.heading: 14. Management
exact_section.evidence_summary: Provides clinician-led conservative and pharmacological management choices; no dose-bearing content is mapped into this project.
